newsitem.title: SWEDEN: GOLF-CARD WORRIES BOOST BAKER AND RIVERO.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-CARD WORRIES BOOST BAKER AND RIVERO.

text.p: Two former Ryder Cup players concerned they might lose their European Tour playing cards at the end of the year raised their games to share the early second round lead in the Scandinavian Masters on Friday.

Spain's Jose Rivero and Englishman Peter Baker set the target of eight-under-par 136, with overnight leader Costantino Rocca of Italy also on the eight-under mark after picking up a shot in three holes of his afternoon round.
Baker, who had to return to the course to finish off the weather-affected first round and birdied his remaining hole, the 18th, shot a 66 while Rivero carded 70.

Both Rivero, who played for Europe in the 1985 and 1987 Ryder Cups, and Baker, a 1993 team member, have their top 40 career money list exemptions expiring at the end of this year and both are currently below the 115th place qualifying mark for next year's card.
Rivero has missed seven of 11 cuts this year and six of the last seven, while Baker has failed to qualify in eight of his last nine outings.
After birdieing the remaining hole of his opening round, Baker, winner of the 1993 Scandinavian Masters, collected seven birdies in his next 11 holes.

"I'm desperate to keep my card and this 66 is a relief," said the Englishman who has had to recover from debilitating glandular fever last year. "It's been a hard job this year because when you're confidence is low you can never see yourself playing well again."
Rivero's round was less spectacular but gave him equal satisfaction. "When you lose your feel like I have over the last two or three months you wonder where you are going," he said.
Jose Maria Olazabal knocked out a spectator during his morning round, his third shot at the 12th ricocheting off the fan's head into a bush.
Olazabal was forced to take a penalty drop and ran up a double bogey on his way to a 74, dropping him back to one under.
